must still match a real symbol — a stale exemption fails the build, so this
cannot become a place gaps go to hide.
documented: the ratchet. It is the exact count the gate expects, so coverage

python.*.__init__: constructors are documented as the class the shell exports (flexiq.Queue, flexiq.TaskConfig), never under the native name
python.PyQueue.check_fan_out_completion: workflow engine internals — flexiq/workflows/ calls these while advancing a run; no user does
python.PyQueue.is_migrated: Queue.__init__ reads it to decide whether state deferred at construction can preload; no public accessor forwards it, and migrate() is the user-facing half
python.PyQueue.count_pending_by_queue: read on the enqueue path by the max_pending admission cap; no public accessor forwards it
python.PyQueue.dead_letters_by_task: declared on the native queue but nothing in the shell forwards it — the Python API lists dead letters unfiltered, via Queue.dead_letters
python.PyQueue.purge_dead_by_task: declared on the native queue but nothing in the shell forwards it — the Python API purges dead letters by age only, via Queue.purge_dead; naming the gap here beats documenting a call no user can make
python.PyResultSender.*: the worker→scheduler result channel; the shell owns every call
python.StepSession.begin_run: step-session plumbing driven by the `step.run` wrapper, not called directly

node.JsQueue.checkFanOutCompletion: workflow engine internals — the shell's workflow runtime calls these while advancing a run
node.JsQueue.compensationNodeForJob: saga engine internals — the compensation leg is driven for the shell, not by it
node.JsQueue.getWorkflowRunPlan: workflow engine internals — the run plan is the scheduler's view of a run, not a shell query
node.JsQueue.workflowNodeForJob: workflow engine internals — maps a job back to its node while advancing a run
node.JsStepSession.beginRun: step-session plumbing driven by the `step.run` wrapper, not called directly
